To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Facebook use increased substantially over the course of the study; (b) body image concerns increased substantially over the same period; (c) number of Facebook friends was a prospective predictor of drive for thinness (i.e. a predictor that was measured at one time point and predicted the outcome at a later time point); and (d) internalisation and body scrutiny predicted the increase in Facebook friendships.

the increase in body image concern over the two year period was prospectively predicted by the increase in the number of Facebook friends, and that the increase in the amount of time spent on Facebook was prospectively predicted the increase in internalization of the thin-ideal and body surveillance.
the number of Facebook friends is a predictor of body image concerns, whereas body image concerns are a predictor of the number of Facebook ‘friends’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how social media use may impact on adolescent body image concerns, which are a major risk factor for the development of eating disorders.
the role that Facebook may play in the body image development of adolescent girls.
understanding the relationship between Facebook and body image in adolescent girls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Facebook use in adolescent girls is a powerful and pervasive social influence on body image.
adolescent girls’ Facebook consumption is associated with increased body image concerns, but that the relationship may be reciprocal.

adolescent girls who are highly involved with Facebook, and who are more likely to be concerned with thinness, will become more concerned with body image over time, and that this is due to a greater number of Facebook friends and a greater tendency to compare themselves to others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more a girl is involved in Facebook, and the more she is concerned with her body, the greater her risk of developing a negative body image.
girls who are more concerned about their bodies and who are more focused on the appearance of others, are more likely to spend more time on Facebook and to have more Facebook friends.
Facebook is a double-edged sword for adolescent girls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Facebook is not the cause of body image concerns, but it does seem to be a potent force for maintaining body image concerns in adolescent girls.
the relationship between Facebook use and the body image of young girls is a two-way street.
the body image of young girls is being shaped by Facebook.
